page.layout: One page of text: running head at the top; verse poem in the centre; a large display fragment "ILLV" at the lower right. No margin notes.

p.i: Commissumque tibi (dicant fortasis) alumnum / Nobis, Geneua, reddito?
At vos lugubri vobis quoque voce Geneua / Audite quid respondeat,
Testor, ait, coeli verum mihi numen amicum, / Legesque testor patrias,
Displicuit facinus, quantum iustisque piisque / Par displicere ciuibus.
Nec culpa hic nostra sceleratus viuit inultus, / Vindicem habiturus alterum:
Quinetiam haec fanti caelesti ex arce Guilelmo, / Vos, o parentes, credite,
Ne me, ne iuuenem indigna ceu morte peremptum, / Auus paterque, plangite:
Caelorum at potius subito sic arce recepto, / Vterque gratulamini.
Namque pius, ferro, placida seu morte, quiescam / Iuuenes, senesve mortui,
Quae vitam hanc miseram lux terminat, hac [?] / mul aui [?] / Vsum perennis inchoat.

page.notes: Long s in the italic verse is printed as a long-s form and is transcribed as plain s. The line ending "hac" and the fragment "mul aui" at the start of the following line are doubtful. "ILLV" is large display type, probably the opening of a word cut off at the scan edge. The second line of the poem has a wavy mark over "Geneua"; this is a stain or pen mark and is not transcribed. Stray marks and specks on the page are not transcribed.
